QuestionStmt.S: If standard emf of cell $\mathrm{Zn_{(s)} | Zn^{2+}_{(1M)} || Ag^+_{(1M)} | Ag_{(s)}}$ is 1.55 V. What is electrical work done under standard conditions?

Solution.S:
Given:

Standard emf of cell, $E_{\text{cell}}^\circ = 1.55$ V

Cell: $\mathrm{Zn_{(s)} | Zn^{2+}_{(1M)} || Ag^+_{(1M)} | Ag_{(s)}}$

Step 1: Write the cell reaction and find $n$

At anode (oxidation):
$$\mathrm{Zn(s) \rightarrow Zn^{2+}(aq) + 2e^-}$$

At cathode (reduction):
$$\mathrm{Ag^+(aq) + e^- \rightarrow Ag(s)}$$

To balance electrons, multiply the cathode reaction by 2:
$$\mathrm{2Ag^+(aq) + 2e^- \rightarrow 2Ag(s)}$$

Overall cell reaction:
$$\mathrm{Zn(s) + 2Ag^+(aq) \rightarrow Zn^{2+}(aq) + 2Ag(s)}$$

So, number of electrons transferred, $n = 2$.

Step 2: Formula for maximum electrical work

Electrical work done under standard conditions is:
$$\Delta G^\circ = -n F E_{\text{cell}}^\circ$$

Where,
$n =$ number of moles of electrons exchanged ($= 2$)
$F =$ Faraday's constant ($= 96500$ C/mol)
$E_{\text{cell}}^\circ =$ emf of the cell ($= 1.55$ V)

Step 3: Substitute and calculate

$$\Delta G^\circ = -2 \times 96500 \times 1.55$$

$$\Delta G^\circ = -2 \times 149575 = -299150 \text{ J}$$

Convert J to kJ:

$$\Delta G^\circ = \frac{-299150}{1000} \text{ kJ} = -299.15 \text{ kJ}$$

The correct answer is: -299.150 kJ
